source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
The Asian citrus psyllid (មមាចលម្អុង) is the insect vector that transmits citrus greening disease (Huanglongbing/HLB) between trees, and it also directly damages trees by sucking nutrients from young shoots.

Spray control options given in the source:
- Imidacloprid 70% SL at 8 ml per 20 L water
- Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5% EC (also listed elsewhere as 2.5% CS) at 15 ml per 20 L water
- Petroleum oil 83.9% EC at 60 ml per 20 L water

Because this insect is the disease vector for citrus greening, controlling it is treated in the source as part of citrus-greening disease management as well as a standalone pest issue -- the same two systemic insecticide options (Imidacloprid, Lambda-cyhalothrin) are repeated under the citrus greening disease entry.
